+###############################################################################
+# Copyright (c) 2026, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. All rights reserved.
+#

+
+"""
+Backport of Megatron-LM #7092 (27f3c8b, "fix(logging): reset log accumulators
+when the first iteration is on a boundary") to the pinned Megatron-LM.
+
+The pinned ``training_log`` sets ``should_reset = not is_first_iteration``: after
+the first iteration of a run it keeps the loss sums, the iteration counters and
+the timers. When that iteration is also a log point (``iteration % log_interval
+== 0``, always with ``log_interval: 1``), the next logged loss and time cover two
+iterations. So a run resumed at iteration N logs N+2 as the mean of N+1 and N+2,
+and its losses do not match an uninterrupted run. Upstream fixed it with
+
+    should_reset = not is_first_iteration or iteration % args.log_interval == 0
+
+With ``reset_log_averages_after_first_log: true`` this patch makes that one-line
+change in the pinned ``training_log`` with ``patch_function_source`` (the line is
+in the middle of the function). Everything else is the pinned code. Only the
+values after the first iteration change (printed loss, and the printed and
+TensorBoard / wandb iteration time and throughput); TensorBoard's loss is
+written per iteration and does not change.
+
+* A Megatron whose ``training_log`` already has upstream #7092 needs no patch:
+  it logs that and does nothing. The fix is recognised by the parsed
+  expression of its one ``should_reset`` assignment (``ast``: spacing, line
+  breaks, parentheses and comments do not matter; the two operands of ``or``
+  and of ``==`` may be in either order). Any other expression is not taken as
+  the fix.
+* Otherwise, when the pinned line is not found, ``should_reset`` is assigned
+  more than once or to another expression, the source cannot be read, or
+  ``training_log`` is not Megatron's function (a wrapper another patch
+  installed: not defined in ``megatron.training.training``), the option cannot
+  be honoured and the patch raises, so a run never silently logs differently from
+  what its config asks for.
+"""
+
+import ast
+import inspect
+import textwrap
+
+from primus.backends.megatron.patches._source_patch_utils import patch_function_source
+from primus.core.patches import PatchContext, get_param, register_patch
+from primus.core.utils.module_utils import log_rank_0
+
+PATCH_ID = "megatron.training_log.first_iteration_reset"
+OPTION = "reset_log_averages_after_first_log"
+PINNED_LINE = "    should_reset = not is_first_iteration\n"
+FIXED_LINE = "    should_reset = not is_first_iteration or iteration % args.log_interval == 0\n"
+_PINNED_EXPR = "not is_first_iteration"
+# Upstream #7092's expression (ast.unparse form), in each operand order.
+_FIXED_EXPRS = {
+    ast.unparse(ast.parse(f"{a} or {b}", mode="eval").body)
+    for x, y in (
+        ("iteration % args.log_interval", "0"),
+        ("0", "iteration % args.log_interval"),
+    )
+    for a, b in ((_PINNED_EXPR, f"{x} == {y}"), (f"{x} == {y}", _PINNED_EXPR))
+}
+
+
+def _should_reset_exprs(source):
+    """The ``ast.unparse`` form of each value assigned to ``should_reset`` in
+    ``source`` (nested functions included). Any other write (an annotated or
+    augmented assignment, ``:=``, a tuple target, a ``for`` / ``with`` / ``del``
+    target) is listed as ``"<other write>"``, so it never matches a known line."""
+    tree = ast.parse(textwrap.dedent(source))
+    plain = {
+        id(node.targets[0]): ast.unparse(node.value)
+        for node in ast.walk(tree)
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and len(node.targets) == 1 and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name)
+    }
+    return [
+        plain.get(id(node), "<other write>")
+        for node in ast.walk(tree)
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id == "should_reset" and not isinstance(node.ctx, ast.Load)
+    ]
+
+
+def check_training_log(training_log, module_name=None):
+    """``"patch"`` when the pinned line can be rewritten, ``"fixed"`` when
+    ``training_log`` already has upstream's fix; ``RuntimeError`` (naming the
+    option) otherwise. ``module_name``: the module ``training_log`` must be
+    defined in (a wrapper installed by another patch is defined elsewhere)."""
+    defined_in = getattr(training_log, "__module__", None)
+    code = getattr(training_log, "__code__", None)
+    if (
+        hasattr(training_log, "__wrapped__")
+        or code is None
+        or (module_name is not None and defined_in != module_name)
+    ):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"{OPTION}: training_log is not Megatron's function ({defined_in}."
+            f"{getattr(training_log, '__qualname__', training_log)!r}), probably a wrapper; the patch "
+            f"{PATCH_ID} must run before other training_log patches, or set {OPTION}: false"
+        )
+    try:
+        source = inspect.getsource(training_log)
+        exprs = _should_reset_exprs(source)
+    except (OSError, TypeError, SyntaxError) as e:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"{OPTION}: cannot read the source of training_log ({e}); set {OPTION}: false"
+        ) from e
+    if len(exprs) == 1 and exprs[0] in _FIXED_EXPRS:
+        return "fixed"
+    if exprs != [_PINNED_EXPR] or source.count(PINNED_LINE) != 1:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"{OPTION}: training_log does not have exactly one should_reset assignment, either "
+            f"{PINNED_LINE.strip()!r} or upstream #7092's fix (found {exprs}); update {PATCH_ID} "
+            f"for this Megatron-LM, or set {OPTION}: false"
+        )
+    return "patch"
+
+
+def apply_backport(module):
+    """Apply the backport to ``module.training_log``; returns ``"patched"`` or
+    ``"fixed"`` (upstream's fix is already there)."""
+    if check_training_log(module.training_log, module.__name__) == "fixed":
+        return "fixed"
+    patch_function_source(module, "training_log", PINNED_LINE, FIXED_LINE)
+    return "patched"
+
+
+def _enabled(ctx: PatchContext) -> bool:
+    return bool(get_param(ctx, OPTION, False))
+
+
+@register_patch(
+    PATCH_ID,
+    backend="megatron",
+    phase="before_train",
+    description="Backport Megatron-LM #7092: reset the log accumulators and timers after a first "
+    "iteration that is a log point.",
+    condition=_enabled,
+    # Before the other training_log wrappers (mlperf 15, print_rank_last 50): it
+    # rewrites Megatron's function itself, whose source they would hide.
+    priority=10,
+)
+def patch_first_iteration_reset(ctx: PatchContext):
+    import megatron.training.training as megatron_training
+
+    from primus.backends.megatron.patches._patch_guard import is_patched, mark_patched
+
+    if is_patched(megatron_training, PATCH_ID):
+        return
+    if apply_backport(megatron_training) == "fixed":

+Standard library only: the posttrain conversion hook loads this file by path
+(without importing ``primus.backends.megatron``, torch or Megatron) to decide
+between the native converter and Megatron-Bridge, and ``native_loader_llama``
+uses the same functions, so the hook and the converter cannot disagree.
+
+Config values are read as HF's ``LlamaConfig`` / ``MistralConfig`` read them,
+with one exception: an absent Llama ``rms_norm_eps`` is 1e-5
+(``LLAMA_FALLBACK_RMS_NORM_EPS``; Llama 2/3 configs set it), not LlamaConfig's
+1e-6. In addition:
+
+* the model shape (``hidden_size``, ``num_attention_heads``,
+  ``num_hidden_layers``, ``intermediate_size``) must be set: the converter does
+  not take the class defaults for the shape of the weights it copies;
+* any other absent key takes that class's default;
+* null is accepted where the class maps it to a value or to "none":
+  ``num_key_value_heads`` (MHA), ``head_dim`` (hidden_size / heads),
+  ``sliding_window`` (no window), ``rope_scaling`` / ``rope_parameters`` (no
+  scaling), ``attention_bias`` / ``mlp_bias`` (no bias), and ``architectures`` /
+  ``model_type`` (read as absent; the other one names the family); any other null
+  is rejected, ``rope_type: null`` included;
+* a value must have the class's type (``attention_bias``, ``mlp_bias`` and
+  ``tie_word_embeddings`` true or false, sizes positive integers);
+* RoPE is read from transformers 5.x ``rope_parameters`` or from the legacy
+  top-level ``rope_theta`` / ``rope_scaling``; a config with both must have
+  the same theta and the same scaling;
+* ``llama3`` scaling (Llama only) needs every HF llama3 key, a ``factor`` of
+  at least 1 (as HF), and the low / high frequency factors and original context
+  Megatron fixes (1 / 4 / 8192, ``MEGATRON_LLAMA3_ROPE_FIXED``);
+* every ``architectures`` entry must be ``LlamaForCausalLM`` or
+  ``MistralForCausalLM`` (one family), and ``model_type``, when set, must name
+  the same family; without ``architectures`` the family comes from ``model_type``;
+* a Mistral config needs ``sliding_window: null``. A window is not modelled:
+  Megatron trains with full causal attention, also past the window when
+  seq_length is longer.
+"""
+
+import math
+
+MISTRAL_NAMES = ("mistral", "mistralforcausallm")
+LLAMA_NAMES = ("llama", "llamaforcausallm")
+
+# Defaults for a config without the key. Mistral uses MistralConfig's defaults;
+# Llama keeps 1e-5 (Llama 2/3 configs set it), not LlamaConfig's 1e-6.
+LLAMA_FALLBACK_RMS_NORM_EPS = 1e-5
+HF_DEFAULT_ROPE_THETA = 10000.0
+HF_DEFAULT_MISTRAL_RMS_NORM_EPS = 1e-6
+HF_DEFAULT_MISTRAL_SLIDING_WINDOW = 4096
+HF_DEFAULT_MISTRAL_KV_HEADS = 8
+HF_DEFAULT_MISTRAL_MAX_POSITION_EMBEDDINGS = 131072
+HF_DEFAULT_LLAMA_MAX_POSITION_EMBEDDINGS = 2048
+
+# RoPE types the converter accepts. The conversion only copies weights; RoPE
+# scaling changes no weight. "llama3" (Llama 3.1/3.2/3.3) is accepted for Llama
+# configs, but the training config must apply it (use_rope_scaling and
+# rope_scaling_factor; Megatron fixes the other llama3 parameters to
+# MEGATRON_LLAMA3_ROPE_FIXED): the conversion hook passes HF's factor to the
+# training run (llama3_rope_scaling). Mistral accepts only no scaling.
+LLAMA_ROPE_TYPES = ("default", "llama3")
+MISTRAL_ROPE_TYPES = ("default",)
+# The llama3 RoPE parameters Megatron does not read from the training config
+# (megatron/core/models/common/embeddings/rotary_pos_embedding.py, _apply_scaling).
+# They are also HF's values for Llama 3.1 / 3.2 / 3.3.
+MEGATRON_LLAMA3_ROPE_FIXED = {
+    "low_freq_factor": 1,
+    "high_freq_factor": 4,
+    "original_max_position_embeddings": 8192,

+class _Unsupported(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def config_names(cfg):
+    """The lower-cased ``architectures`` entries and ``model_type`` of an HF config.
+    ``ValueError`` when ``architectures`` is not a string or a list of strings."""
+    architectures = cfg.get("architectures") or []
+    if isinstance(architectures, str):
+        architectures = [architectures]
+    if not isinstance(architectures, list) or not all(isinstance(a, str) for a in architectures):
+        raise ValueError(f"architectures {architectures!r} (a list of strings is required)")
+    return [a.lower() for a in architectures] + [str(cfg.get("model_type", "")).lower()]
+
+
+def _family_of(name):
+    return "mistral" if name in MISTRAL_NAMES else "llama" if name in LLAMA_NAMES else None

+
+def config_family(cfg):
+    """``"llama"`` | ``"mistral"`` | None. Every ``architectures`` entry must be a
+    Llama or Mistral causal LM of one family, and ``model_type`` (when set) must
+    name that family; without ``architectures`` the family is ``model_type``'s.
+    ``_Unsupported`` when the names conflict (for example ``Qwen2ForCausalLM``
+    with ``model_type: llama``, or ``LlamaForSequenceClassification``); None
+    when nothing names Llama or Mistral."""
+    try:
+        names = config_names(cfg)
+    except ValueError as e:
+        raise _Unsupported(str(e)) from None
+    architectures = names[:-1]
+    model_type = names[-1] if names[-1] not in ("", "none") else None

+        return _family_of(model_type)
+    arch_families = {_family_of(n) for n in architectures}
+    if arch_families == {None} and _family_of(model_type) is None:
+        return None  # another model: not this converter's
+    if None in arch_families or len(arch_families) > 1:
+        raise _Unsupported(
+            f"architectures {architectures} (only LlamaForCausalLM or MistralForCausalLM: "
+            "not other models, heads, or both)"
+        )
+    family = arch_families.pop()
+    if model_type is not None and _family_of(model_type) != family:
+        raise _Unsupported(f"architectures/model_type {names} (they name different models)")
+    return family
+

+def llama3_rope_scaling(cfg):
+    """The ``llama3`` RoPE scaling parameters of a config (``rope_parameters`` or
+    ``rope_scaling``; ``_rope`` requires the two to agree), or None. The converter
+    copies weights only; the conversion hook passes the scaling to the training
+    run."""
+    for key in ("rope_parameters", "rope_scaling"):
+        params = cfg.get(key)
+        if isinstance(params, dict) and params.get("rope_type", params.get("type")) == "llama3":
+            return params
+    return None
+
+
+def llama3_rope_problem(params):
+    """Why Megatron's llama3 RoPE scaling cannot reproduce these ``llama3``
+    parameters, or None. As HF (``_validate_llama3_parameters``), every key is
+    required and ``factor`` is at least 1; Megatron has an option only for
+    ``factor`` and fixes the others (``MEGATRON_LLAMA3_ROPE_FIXED``)."""
+    factor = params.get("factor")
+    try:
+        ok = (
+            not isinstance(factor, bool)
+            and isinstance(factor, (int, float))
+            and 1 <= float(factor) < math.inf
+        )

+        ok = False
+    if not ok:
+        return f"factor {factor!r} (a finite number of at least 1 is required)"

+        if name not in params:
+            return f"{name} missing (HF requires it; Megatron's llama3 RoPE scaling uses {fixed})"

+    return None

+
+def _int(key, value):
+    """A positive integer; an integral float (JSON ``4096.0``) is accepted."""
+    if isinstance(value, float) and value.is_integer():

+    if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0:
+        return value
+    raise _Unsupported(f"{key} {value!r} (a positive integer is required)")

+def _number(key, value):

+            )

+        raise _Unsupported(f"rope_parameters {rope_parameters!r} and rope_scaling {rope_scaling!r} differ")
+    thetas = {
+        float(_number(label, d["rope_theta"]))
+        for label, d in (("rope_theta", cfg), ("rope_parameters.rope_theta", rope_parameters or {}))
+        if "rope_theta" in d

+    # is MistralConfig's 8 for Mistral and MHA for Llama.
+    if mistral and "num_key_value_heads" not in cfg:

+            raise _Unsupported(
+                f"hidden_size {hidden} is not a multiple of num_attention_heads {heads} (and no head_dim)"
+            )
+        head_dim = hidden // heads
+    else:
+        head_dim = _int("head_dim", cfg["head_dim"])
+    eps = _number(
+        "rms_norm_eps",
+        _present(
+            cfg, "rms_norm_eps", HF_DEFAULT_MISTRAL_RMS_NORM_EPS if mistral else LLAMA_FALLBACK_RMS_NORM_EPS
+        ),
+    )
+    act = _present(cfg, "hidden_act", "silu")
+    if act not in ("silu", "swish"):
+        raise _Unsupported(f"{label} hidden_act {act!r} (only SwiGLU with silu)")

+    if not isinstance(tie, bool):
+        raise _Unsupported(f"tie_word_embeddings {tie!r} (true or false is required)")

+    window = cfg.get("sliding_window", HF_DEFAULT_MISTRAL_SLIDING_WINDOW)

+        raise _Unsupported(
+            f"Mistral sliding_window {window!r} (only full causal attention: sliding_window: null)"
+        )
+
+    return dict(
+        hidden_size=hidden,
+        num_attention_heads=heads,
+        num_layers=layers,
+        max_position_embeddings=max_pos,
+        norm_epsilon=eps,
+        rotary_base=theta,

+    )

+    """Why the native Llama converter cannot convert this HF config, or None when it can."""
+    try:
+        _fields(cfg)
+    except _Unsupported as e:
+        return str(e)
+    return None
+
+
+def derive_megatron_fields(cfg):
+    """Megatron arg values for a supported Llama (2/3/3.x) or dense Mistral HF
+    config; ``ValueError`` with ``unsupported_reason`` otherwise."""
+    try:
+        return _fields(cfg)
+    except _Unsupported as e:
+        raise ValueError(f"native Llama converter: config not supported: {e}") from None

+"""
+Backport of Megatron-LM #7092 (27f3c8b, "fix(logging): reset log accumulators
+when the first iteration is on a boundary") to the pinned Megatron-LM.
+
+The pinned ``training_log`` sets ``should_reset = not is_first_iteration``: after
+the first iteration of a run it keeps the loss sums, the iteration counters and
+the timers. When that iteration is also a log point (``iteration % log_interval
+== 0``, always with ``log_interval: 1``), the next logged loss and time cover two
+iterations. So a run resumed at iteration N logs N+2 as the mean of N+1 and N+2,
+and its losses do not match an uninterrupted run. Upstream fixed it with
+
+    should_reset = not is_first_iteration or iteration % args.log_interval == 0
+
+With ``reset_log_averages_after_first_log: true`` this patch makes that one-line
+change in the pinned ``training_log`` with ``patch_function_source`` (the line is
+in the middle of the function). Everything else is the pinned code. Only the
+values after the first iteration change (printed loss, and the printed and
+TensorBoard / wandb iteration time and throughput); TensorBoard's loss is
+written per iteration and does not change.
+
+* A Megatron whose ``training_log`` already has upstream #7092 needs no patch:
+  it logs that and does nothing. The fix is recognised by the parsed
+  expression of its one ``should_reset`` assignment (``ast``: spacing, line
+  breaks, parentheses and comments do not matter; the two operands of ``or``
+  and of ``==`` may be in either order). Any other expression is not taken as
+  the fix.
+* Otherwise, when the pinned line is not found, ``should_reset`` is assigned
+  more than once or to another expression, the source cannot be read, or
+  ``training_log`` is not Megatron's function (a wrapper another patch
+  installed: not defined in ``megatron.training.training``), the option cannot
+  be honoured and the patch raises, so a run never silently logs differently from
+  what its config asks for.
+"""

+import inspect
+import textwrap
+
+from primus.backends.megatron.patches._source_patch_utils import patch_function_source
+from primus.core.patches import PatchContext, get_param, register_patch
+from primus.core.utils.module_utils import log_rank_0
+
+PATCH_ID = "megatron.training_log.first_iteration_reset"
+OPTION = "reset_log_averages_after_first_log"
+PINNED_LINE = "    should_reset = not is_first_iteration\n"
+FIXED_LINE = "    should_reset = not is_first_iteration or iteration % args.log_interval == 0\n"
+_PINNED_EXPR = "not is_first_iteration"

+_FIXED_EXPRS = {
+    ast.unparse(ast.parse(f"{a} or {b}", mode="eval").body)
+    for x, y in (
+        ("iteration % args.log_interval", "0"),
+        ("0", "iteration % args.log_interval"),
+    )
+    for a, b in ((_PINNED_EXPR, f"{x} == {y}"), (f"{x} == {y}", _PINNED_EXPR))

+    ``source`` (nested functions included). Any other write (an annotated or
+    augmented assignment, ``:=``, a tuple target, a ``for`` / ``with`` / ``del``
+    target) is listed as ``"<other write>"``, so it never matches a known line."""
+    tree = ast.parse(textwrap.dedent(source))
+    plain = {
+        id(node.targets[0]): ast.unparse(node.value)
+        for node in ast.walk(tree)
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and len(node.targets) == 1 and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name)
+    }
+    return [
+        plain.get(id(node), "<other write>")
+        for node in ast.walk(tree)

+# Weight mapping on a tiny synthetic Mistral-shaped checkpoint
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+class _Store:
+    def __init__(self, tensors):
+        self.t = tensors
+        self.reads = []
+
+    def get(self, name, dtype):
+        self.reads.append(name)
+        return self.t[name].to(dtype)
+
+    def has(self, name):
+        return name in self.t
+

+def _tiny(vocab=200, padded=256):
+    torch = pytest.importorskip("torch")
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+    hidden, nh, ng, ffn, layers = 64, 8, 2, 96, 2
+    hd = hidden // nh
+    r = lambda *s: torch.randn(*s, generator=g)  # noqa: E731
+    t = {
+        "model.embed_tokens.weight": r(vocab, hidden),
+        "model.norm.weight": r(hidden),
+        "lm_head.weight": r(vocab, hidden),
+    }
+    for L in range(layers):
+        h = f"model.layers.{L}."
+        t[h + "input_layernorm.weight"] = r(hidden)
+        t[h + "post_attention_layernorm.weight"] = r(hidden)
+        t[h + "self_attn.q_proj.weight"] = r(nh * hd, hidden)
+        t[h + "self_attn.k_proj.weight"] = r(ng * hd, hidden)
+        t[h + "self_attn.v_proj.weight"] = r(ng * hd, hidden)
+        t[h + "self_attn.o_proj.weight"] = r(hidden, nh * hd)
+        t[h + "mlp.gate_proj.weight"] = r(ffn, hidden)
+        t[h + "mlp.up_proj.weight"] = r(ffn, hidden)
+        t[h + "mlp.down_proj.weight"] = r(hidden, ffn)
+    cfg = dict(
+        MISTRAL_V03,
+        hidden_size=hidden,
+        num_attention_heads=nh,
+        num_key_value_heads=ng,
+        intermediate_size=ffn,
+        num_hidden_layers=layers,
+        vocab_size=vocab,
+    )
+    fields = _rules().derive_megatron_fields(cfg)
+    margs = SimpleNamespace(
+        params_dtype=torch.float32,
+        num_attention_heads=nh,
+        num_query_groups=fields["num_query_groups"],
+        kv_channels=fields["kv_channels"],
+        hidden_size=hidden,
+        num_layers=layers,
+        untie_embeddings_and_output_weights=fields["untie_embeddings_and_output_weights"],
+    )
+    model = SimpleNamespace(
+        state_dict=lambda: {"embedding.word_embeddings.weight": torch.empty(padded, hidden)}
+    )
+    return torch, t, fields, margs, model, (nh, ng, hd, hidden)
+

+def test_weight_mapping_round_trip():

+"""
+Backport of Megatron-LM #7092 (27f3c8b, "fix(logging): reset log accumulators
+when the first iteration is on a boundary") to the pinned Megatron-LM.
+
+The pinned ``training_log`` sets ``should_reset = not is_first_iteration``: after
+the first iteration of a run it keeps the loss sums, the iteration counters and
+the timers. When that iteration is also a log point (``iteration % log_interval
+== 0``, always with ``log_interval: 1``), the next logged loss and time cover two
+iterations. So a run resumed at iteration N logs N+2 as the mean of N+1 and N+2,
+and its losses do not match an uninterrupted run. Upstream fixed it with
+
+    should_reset = not is_first_iteration or iteration % args.log_interval == 0
+
+With ``reset_log_averages_after_first_log: true`` this patch makes that one-line
+change in the pinned ``training_log`` with ``patch_function_source`` (the line is
+in the middle of the function). Everything else is the pinned code. Only the
+values after the first iteration change (printed loss, and the printed and
+TensorBoard / wandb iteration time and throughput); TensorBoard's loss is
+written per iteration and does not change.
+
+* A Megatron whose ``training_log`` already has upstream #7092 needs no patch:
+  it logs that and does nothing. The fix is recognised by the parsed
+  expression of its one ``should_reset`` assignment (``ast``: spacing, line
+  breaks, parentheses and comments do not matter; the two operands of ``or``
+  and of ``==`` may be in either order). Any other expression is not taken as
+  the fix.
+* Otherwise, when the pinned line is not found, ``should_reset`` is assigned
+  more than once or to another expression, the source cannot be read, or
+  ``training_log`` is not Megatron's function (a wrapper another patch
+  installed: not defined in ``megatron.training.training``), the option cannot
+  be honoured and the patch raises, so a run never silently logs differently from
+  what its config asks for.
+"""

+import ast
+import inspect
+import textwrap
+
+from primus.backends.megatron.patches._source_patch_utils import patch_function_source
+from primus.core.patches import PatchContext, get_param, register_patch
+from primus.core.utils.module_utils import log_rank_0
+
+PATCH_ID = "megatron.training_log.first_iteration_reset"
+OPTION = "reset_log_averages_after_first_log"
+PINNED_LINE = "    should_reset = not is_first_iteration\n"
+FIXED_LINE = "    should_reset = not is_first_iteration or iteration % args.log_interval == 0\n"
+_PINNED_EXPR = "not is_first_iteration"
+# Upstream #7092's expression (ast.unparse form), in each operand order.
+_FIXED_EXPRS = {
+    ast.unparse(ast.parse(f"{a} or {b}", mode="eval").body)
+    for x, y in (
+        ("iteration % args.log_interval", "0"),
+        ("0", "iteration % args.log_interval"),
+    )
+    for a, b in ((_PINNED_EXPR, f"{x} == {y}"), (f"{x} == {y}", _PINNED_EXPR))
+}
+
+
+def _should_reset_exprs(source):
+    """The ``ast.unparse`` form of each value assigned to ``should_reset`` in
+    ``source`` (nested functions included). Any other write (an annotated or
+    augmented assignment, ``:=``, a tuple target, a ``for`` / ``with`` / ``del``
+    target) is listed as ``"<other write>"``, so it never matches a known line."""
+    tree = ast.parse(textwrap.dedent(source))
+    plain = {
+        id(node.targets[0]): ast.unparse(node.value)
+        for node in ast.walk(tree)
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and len(node.targets) == 1 and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name)
+    }
+    return [
+        plain.get(id(node), "<other write>")
+        for node in ast.walk(tree)
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id == "should_reset" and not isinstance(node.ctx, ast.Load)
+    ]
+
+
+def check_training_log(training_log, module_name=None):
+    """``"patch"`` when the pinned line can be rewritten, ``"fixed"`` when
+    ``training_log`` already has upstream's fix; ``RuntimeError`` (naming the
+    option) otherwise. ``module_name``: the module ``training_log`` must be
+    defined in (a wrapper installed by another patch is defined elsewhere)."""
+    defined_in = getattr(training_log, "__module__", None)
+    code = getattr(training_log, "__code__", None)
+    if (
+        hasattr(training_log, "__wrapped__")
+        or code is None
+        or (module_name is not None and defined_in != module_name)
+    ):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"{OPTION}: training_log is not Megatron's function ({defined_in}."
+            f"{getattr(training_log, '__qualname__', training_log)!r}), probably a wrapper; the patch "
+            f"{PATCH_ID} must run before other training_log patches, or set {OPTION}: false"
+        )
+    try:
+        source = inspect.getsource(training_log)
+        exprs = _should_reset_exprs(source)
+    except (OSError, TypeError, SyntaxError) as e:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"{OPTION}: cannot read the source of training_log ({e}); set {OPTION}: false"
+        ) from e
+    if len(exprs) == 1 and exprs[0] in _FIXED_EXPRS:
+        return "fixed"
+    if exprs != [_PINNED_EXPR] or source.count(PINNED_LINE) != 1:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"{OPTION}: training_log does not have exactly one should_reset assignment, either "
+            f"{PINNED_LINE.strip()!r} or upstream #7092's fix (found {exprs}); update {PATCH_ID} "
+            f"for this Megatron-LM, or set {OPTION}: false"
+        )
+    return "patch"
+

+    ``"fixed"`` (upstream's fix is already there)."""
+    if check_training_log(module.training_log, module.__name__) == "fixed":
+        return "fixed"

+
